source.title: Dynamics of stochastic gradient descent for two-layer neural networks in the teacher–student setup
source.authors: Sebastian Goldt; Madhu S. Advani; Andrew M. Saxe; Florent Krzakala; L. Zdeborová

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplemental material are present; no apparent cutoff or garbling affecting the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how over-parameterization and training choices affect generalization in a teacher–student setting using two-layer networks and regression error, rather than the claim versions’ natural-label classification setup.
record.gate_note: Own results concern generalization error relative to a teacher, with noisy teacher outputs; these do not test memorization of random labels or the listed natural-label classification claims. Rows capture reported comparisons of network size, trained layers, activation, mini-batch size, input data, training-set size, and weight decay. Figures used where exact numeric values are not stated in text are recorded as figure only. The cited prior studies are not extracted as results.
record.test_reason: The study measures teacher–student regression error as student width exceeds teacher width. It does not establish widening beyond a zero-training-error threshold, as V2 requires. Its batch experiments measure asymptotic error without a fixed epoch budget, so they do not test V5. None of its own results measures the other versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: generalization depends jointly on SGD dynamics, architecture, and data. With noisy teacher outputs, training only the first layer makes error increase with width; training both layers decreases it for sigmoidal networks and leaves it approximately constant for linear and ReLU networks. These conclusions concern teacher–student regression.
record.recipe_differences: Analyzes online SGD in finite-hidden-unit two-layer teacher–student regression with noisy teacher outputs and generalisation error over the input distribution; not the claim versions’ natural-label classification or train–test gap measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The result changes with activation function, which layers are trainable, student width, learning rate, mini-batch size, weight decay, and finite training-set size; input choice between Gaussian and MNIST images showed good agreement in the tested setup.

fits_no_version.finding: With noisy teacher outputs and only the first layer trained, asymptotic regression error grows with excess student width; learning-rate scaling does not eliminate this trend.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Over-parameterization relative to teacher complexity can worsen online regression generalization under fixed output weights.

fits_no_version.finding: Training both layers makes error decrease with width for sigmoidal networks and remain approximately constant for linear and ReLU networks; output-weight normalization also reduces error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Width effects in teacher–student regression depend on activation, trainable layers, and effective learning rate.

fits_no_version.finding: Weight decay did not improve the tested asymptotic errors; larger mini-batches reduced error until gains became minimal.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Regularization and batch-size effects in online teacher–student regression differ from fixed-budget classification comparisons.

fits_no_version.finding: MNIST and Gaussian input comparisons agreed, while reducing finite training-set size could shift the best nonlinear student width above teacher width.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-set size changes the width–generalization relationship in teacher–student regression.

record.problems: Teacher–student synthetic regression with Gaussian output noise is not natural-label classification or a direct training-versus-test error gap. Many trends are shown in figures without text giving exact values; some experiments rely on a single run, while the Figure 4 and Figure S8 uncertainty is reported as standard deviation.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Cited results from prior work were excluded.

untested.parts: Fixed random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond an established zero-training-error threshold in the stated classification setting.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classification and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, including tuning and optimizer adaptations.
Batch-size penalties under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove them.
Dropout effects and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions; this does not dispute the reported regression trends. Excess teacher width K−M is not an established training-set interpolation threshold.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization coexisting with natural-label classification generalization; listed models and datasets.
One-hidden-layer ReLU networks on MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10, widening past interpolation; the study uses two-layer teacher–student regression.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD/momentum on image and language benchmarks.
Large-batch effects under fixed epoch budgets on image classifiers and language models, including recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects on held-out classification error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to train–test gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: sigmoidal Soft Committee Machine student
rows.operation_detail: Varied student hidden-unit count while training only the first layer; measured final generalisation error with noisy teacher outputs.

conditions.value: online SGD; second-layer weights fixed at 1

rows.value: With all else equal, error increases linearly with L; small-learning-rate expression is σ²η/(2π)(L + M/√3) + O(η²).
rows.note: Teacher–student regression generalisation error, not train–test classification error. Text reports theoretical prediction in excellent agreement with a single SGD run.
rows.check: The width threshold is teacher size, not interpolation of a fixed training set. The small-learning-rate formula is Eq. (11); Eq. (14) states the scaling.

rows.subject: linear Soft Committee Machine student
rows.operation_detail: Varied student hidden-unit count while training only the first layer; measured final generalisation error.

conditions.value: online SGD; second-layer weights fixed at 1

rows.value: ϵ*g = ησ²(L + M)/(4 − 2η(L + M)) + O(σ³); at small η, error scales as ησ²(L + M)/4.
rows.note: Paper states theoretical result is in perfect agreement with experiments.
rows.check: Linear teacher–student regression does not measure V2's widening beyond zero training error.

rows.subject: ReLU Soft Committee Machine student
rows.operation_detail: Varied student hidden-unit count while training only the first layer; measured asymptotic generalisation error.
rows.locator: Section 2; Figure S3; Supplemental Section G
rows.note: Text says simulations confirm the stated scaling; no exact values are given.
rows.check: Despite using ReLU networks, this measures online regression beyond teacher width, without an established interpolation threshold.

rows.subject: sigmoidal two-layer student
rows.operation_detail: Varied student width while training both layers; measured asymptotic generalisation error.
rows.value: Increasing K decreases the asymptotic error.
rows.note: Study reports learning dynamics and the width trend; the statement concerns teacher–student regression.
rows.check: Decreasing teacher–student error beyond teacher width does not establish V2's post-interpolation effect.

rows.subject: linear two-layer student
rows.size_stated: K increasing; Figure 4 uses N = 100, M = 4
rows.operation_detail: Varied width while training both layers and compared with fixed-second-layer and normalized variants.

conditions.value: both layers; small random initial weights
SCM and Normalised variants also shown

rows.value: Error remains constant with increasing K when both layers are trained.
rows.uncertainty: Figure 4 error bars are one standard deviation over five runs; values not stated in text.
rows.note: Text says constant with K; comparison with the 1/K decay of sigmoidal networks is explicitly made.
rows.check: Constant regression error in linear networks is not a partial observation of any listed version.

rows.subject: ReLU two-layer student
rows.size_stated: K increasing; supplemental Figure S4 uses N = 500, M = 2
rows.operation_detail: Varied width while training both layers; measured asymptotic generalisation error.
rows.value: Error remains constant with increasing K.
rows.uncertainty: Figure S4 error bars are one standard deviation over five runs; values not stated in text.
rows.note: Text reports qualitatively similar features to linear networks.
rows.check: Constant online regression error does not establish the presence or absence of V2's post-interpolation effect.

rows.subject: normalised Soft Committee Machine student
rows.operation_detail: Varied width with second-layer weights fixed to 1/K; measured asymptotic error.

conditions.value: first layer trained; second-layer weights fixed at 1/K

rows.uncertainty: Figure 4 error bars are one standard deviation over five runs; values not stated in text.
rows.note: Authors attribute the trend to the fixed second-layer weights effectively reducing the learning rate.
rows.check: Normalization changes effective learning rate, without testing interpolation. Specify that teacher second-layer weights are also normalized to 1/M.

rows.subject: sigmoidal Soft Committee Machine student
rows.operation_detail: Added weight decay to SGD and compared final generalisation error with no weight decay.

conditions.value: first layer trained; second-layer weights fixed

rows.value: No tested setup improved the error; weight decay failed to mitigate the increase with L, and error increased with κ in the illustrative experiment.
rows.note: Authors explicitly state they found no setup where weight decay improved asymptotic error.
rows.check: Weight decay alone in synthetic regression does not test V6's dropout claim or its joint-removal condition.

rows.subject: sigmoidal Soft Committee Machine student
rows.operation_detail: Varied mini-batch size and student width; measured asymptotic generalisation error.
rows.baseline: batch size 1 (online learning) shown as a reference curve
rows.value: Increasing batch size decreases error up to a point, after which gains are minimal; the error-versus-L curve has the same shape for all batch sizes, with minimum at K = M.
rows.note: Study's batch-size effect is on teacher–student regression error, not fixed-epoch image or language classification.
rows.check: Asymptotic mini-batch comparisons lack V5's fixed epoch budget; larger batches use more fresh samples per update. Figure S6 also reports ReLU networks, omitted from this row.

rows.subject: Soft Committee Machine student on Gaussian inputs
rows.operation_detail: Compared Gaussian inputs with MNIST images as inputs to the same teacher–student regression setup.
rows.value: MNIST-image and Gaussian-input curves are in good agreement.
rows.note: MNIST labels are not used; this is regression with teacher-generated labels.
rows.check: MNIST images supply inputs, not natural classification labels. Section G.3 compares finite MNIST and Gaussian datasets of the same size; describing this as strictly online learning obscures sample reuse.

rows.subject: linear student
rows.operation_detail: Reduced the finite training set size and measured final generalisation error versus excess width.

conditions.value: P = 4 or P = 50 samples per input dimension N

rows.value: Larger networks perform worse for both P = 4 and P = 50; optimum is K = 1.
rows.uncertainty: Figure S8 error bars indicate one standard deviation over 10 simulations; many too small to see.
rows.note: The text states P samples are scaled by N in the figure description.
rows.check: Finite-set linear regression does not test V2. State explicitly that only the first layer is trained; P denotes the multiplier in PN training samples.

rows.subject: sigmoidal student
rows.operation_detail: Varied finite training set size and width; measured final generalisation error.

conditions.value: P = 4 or P = 50 samples per input dimension N
finite data set; repeated sample visits

rows.value: At P = 50, best generalisation is at K = M; at P = 4, best generalisation is at K > M.
rows.uncertainty: Figure S8 error bars indicate one standard deviation over 10 simulations; many too small to see.
rows.note: Authors say finite-data behavior varies with set size; early-stopping error shows qualitatively the same behavior.
rows.check: An optimum above teacher width does not establish improvement beyond interpolation. Only the first layer is trained, and the training-set sizes are PN.

rows.subject: ReLU student
rows.operation_detail: Varied finite training set size and width; measured final generalisation error.

conditions.value: P = 4 or P = 50 samples per input dimension N
finite data set; repeated sample visits

rows.value: At P = 50, best generalisation is at K = M; at P = 4, best generalisation is at K > M.
rows.uncertainty: Figure S8 error bars indicate one standard deviation over 10 simulations; many too small to see.
rows.note: The text groups the large-set and small-set behavior for nonlinear networks; figure displays separate activation panels.
rows.check: The finite-set ReLU result does not identify zero training error or the interpolation width. Only the first layer is trained, and the training-set sizes are PN.

rows.subject: sigmoidal Soft Committee Machine student
rows.operation_detail: Varied learning rate with width; measured asymptotic generalisation error.

conditions.value: first layer trained; second-layer weights fixed

rows.value: With η = 1/K, error still increases with L before plateauing at a constant independent of M.
rows.note: Also reported in main-text discussion of Figure S2.
rows.check: Learning-rate scaling in online teacher–student regression does not measure any listed version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
